title: Given a `List<Employee>`, remove exact duplicate objects using `distinct()`, and separately remove duplicates by a key such as id where the objects are not equal. Explain how `distinct()` relies on `equals`/`hashCode` and how to deduplicate by a custom key.
shortTitle: Remove duplicate employees by id using a key-based filter, and remove exact duplicates using distinct
keyPoints: `distinct()` removes duplicates by comparing elements with their `equals` and `hashCode`, so it only works when those methods are correct.
For records, `equals`/`hashCode` cover every component automatically, so `distinct()` drops only objects identical in every field.
To deduplicate by a business key such as id, use a stateful filter backed by a `Set` of seen keys: `filter(e -> seen.add(e.getId()))`.
`Set.add` returns `true` only the first time a key is seen, so the stateful filter keeps the first occurrence per key.
The parallel-safe alternative is `Collectors.toMap(Employee::getId, e -> e, (a, b) -> a)` with a merge function that keeps the first value.
The stateful-filter trick is unsafe in a parallel stream because the shared `Set` makes the result order-dependent and non-deterministic.
`distinct()` on an ordered stream preserves the encounter order of the first occurrence of each element.

s1_definition.oneliner: `distinct()` removes duplicates by `equals`/`hashCode`; to dedupe by a key, track seen keys in a `Set` or collect into a `Map` keyed by that field and keep the first value.
s1_definition.profdef:
Two different jobs look the same but need different tools.

- **`distinct()`** – an intermediate, stateful operation that keeps a set of elements it has already emitted and drops any element that `equals` one already seen.
- **`equals`/`hashCode` dependency** – `distinct()` has no idea what a duplicate means; it delegates that entirely to the element's own `equals` and `hashCode`.
- **Key-based dedup with a stateful filter** – `Set<Long> seen = new HashSet<>(); stream.filter(e -> seen.add(e.getId()))` keeps only the first element per key because `Set.add` returns `true` once per key.
- **Key-based dedup with `toMap`** – `collect(Collectors.toMap(Employee::getId, e -> e, (a, b) -> a))` keeps one value per key and is safe in parallel.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya has a pile of account-opening forms and some are exact photocopies of the same form. `distinct()` throws away the exact photocopies. But sometimes two forms carry the same account number while the name or address differs slightly. To keep just one form per account number she keeps a checklist of numbers she has already filed and skips any form whose number is already ticked.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  distinct()  -- removes EXACT duplicates by equals/hashCode

  [A id=1] [B id=1 same fields] [C id=2]
       │        │                   │
       ▼        ▼                   ▼
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  seen set: {}                          │
  │  A -> not in set -> emit, add A        │
  │  B -> equals A   -> drop               │
  │  C -> not in set -> emit, add C        │
  └───────────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       ▼
  [A id=1] [C id=2]
```

```text
  filter(e -> seen.add(e.getId()))  -- dedup by KEY

  [id=101 Rajesh Kumar] [id=101 Rajesh K.] [id=102 Priya]
           │                    │                 │
           ▼                    ▼                 ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  seen keys: {}                                        │
  │  101 -> add returns true  -> keep                     │
  │  101 -> add returns false -> drop (stale name copy)   │
  │  102 -> add returns true  -> keep                     │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           │
           ▼
  [id=101 Rajesh Kumar] [id=102 Priya]
```

```text
  Choose the tool

  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │ Duplicate = identical fields? │
  └──────────────┬───────────────┘
        yes      │      no
         ▼       │       ▼
   distinct()    │   dedup by key
                 │   ┌────────────┬──────────────┐
                 │   │ sequential │   parallel   │
                 │   ▼            ▼
                 │ stateful     toMap(..., merge)
                 │ filter
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To remove exact duplicate objects from a stream I use `distinct()`, which keeps a set of elements it has already emitted and drops any element that equals one already seen. The crucial point is that `distinct()` relies entirely on the element's `equals` and `hashCode`, so for a record, where both methods cover every component automatically, `distinct()` removes only records that are identical in every field.

In my banking work at the National Bank of India one feed occasionally sent the exact same employee record twice, and a plain `distinct()` cleaned those up perfectly. But a different feed sent two records that shared an employee id where one name was stale, and `distinct()` could not help because those two objects are not equal. For that I deduplicated by the business key: I kept a set of seen ids and filtered the stream with `seen.add(e.getId())`, which returns true only the first time an id appears, so only the first record per id survives.

The senior nuance I always mention is that this stateful filter is not safe in a parallel stream, because the shared set makes the outcome depend on thread timing. When I need parallel-safe deduplication by a key I collect into a map keyed by id with a merge function that keeps the first value, and then take the map's values, which is deterministic regardless of parallelism. That same merge function also lets me decide to keep the higher salary or the latest record instead of the first.

Think of Priya filing account forms: she bins the exact photocopies, and for forms that merely share an account number she keeps a ticked checklist of numbers so each account is filed only once.

Remember one sentence: `distinct()` dedupes by `equals`/`hashCode`, but to dedupe by a key you track seen keys in a `Set` or collect into a `Map` and keep one value per key.
